# ConfigMap and Secret Reload Strategies

> Why the kubelet doesn't restart Pods on CM/Secret content change, and the
> Reloader-direct-mount-only gotcha, live in
> [knowledgebase/kubernetes/configmap-reload.md](https://github.com/jewzaam/knowledgebase/blob/main/kubernetes/configmap-reload.md).

## Strategies, most sustainable first

### 1. Cluster-wide controller (preferred)

Install [stakater/Reloader](https://github.com/stakater/Reloader) once, opt
workloads in by annotation. Reloader watches ConfigMap/Secret events and
patches the consumer Deployment (or StatefulSet, DaemonSet, etc.) to trigger
a rolling restart.

Opt-in annotation on the consumer workload:

```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    reloader.stakater.com/auto: "true"
```

### 2. Per-chart `checksum/configmap` Helm helper

Use a Helm chart's `checksum/config` annotation pattern when running a
single chart and not a cluster controller. Works without an extra
controller but only covers ConfigMaps the chart author opted to hash.

### 3. Manual `kubectl rollout restart`

Defeats GitOps automation and requires human intervention every time
config changes. Use only as an emergency manual override, never as the
documented day-2 procedure.

## When to apply

- Any new workload that consumes a ConfigMap or Secret whose content
  changes during the cluster's lifetime (datasources, scrape configs,
  feature flags, TLS material, sealed-secret-derived credentials).
- Any chart bump where the chart introduces a new ConfigMap the workload
  reads at startup.

## When skipping is acceptable

- ConfigMaps that are only read by init containers (the init runs every
  Pod start, so the next restart picks up the change naturally — though
  the restart still needs a trigger).
- Workloads designed to watch their config file at runtime and reload
  in-process (rare; verify in the upstream docs before assuming).
